header.title: How to Wire a Three Pronged Dryer Plug
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to replace a dryer cord with a three-prong plug, ensuring a safe and functional connection for your dryer.

steps.description: Select a new three-prong cord that is compatible with the existing outlet.
actions: Identify the pattern of the outlet
Select a matching three-prong cord
Refer to Figure 4 to ensure correct cord selection

steps.description: The dryer's electrical access panel is removed to expose the terminal block and wire connections.
actions: Confirm the right cord was picked.
Remove the dryer’s electrical access panel.
Examine the four wire cable.
Observe the black, red, white, and green wires inside.
Identify the green wire connections to the chassis/case for grounding.
Note the difference in green wire connections after cord replacement.

steps.description: Remove screws securing wires to the chassis and terminal block, noting the location of each color.
actions: Remove screws securing the green wires to the chassis
Remove the three wires to the terminal block
Take care not to lose any of the screws
Make note of where each color goes

steps.description: The four wire cable is removed from the dryer after loosening the cable clamp.
actions: loosen the cable clamp
remove the four wire cable from the dryer

steps.description: The new cord is inserted into the freed knockout opening without the cable clamp.
actions: Insert the new cord
Insert into the knockout opening
Do not use the cable clamp at this time

steps.description: Connect the wires from the new three-prong cable to the terminal block, ensuring color matching or proper placement for uncolored cables, and connect the grounding strap.
actions: Attach wires to the terminal block to match the same colored wires from the dryer (if colored).
Connect the grounding strap between the center terminal and the dryer case.
Connect the center wire to the middle terminal screw (if the new cord is a flat cable without color-coding).
Attach the outside wires to each of the outside terminals on the terminal block (if the new cord is a flat cable without color-coding).

steps.description: Secure the cable and access cover to finalize the system setup.
actions: tighten the cable clamp
put back the access cover
screw in the access cover
